propositions: The test kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 because its single monolithic loop iterates 884 renderable units (1768 serial pandoc spawns) with unbounded cost: 91.6s idle, 504.8s under CPU saturation, exceeding CI's 300s per-test guard

pytest-timeout with --timeout-method=thread calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the worker outright with no traceback or assertion, causing the worker to appear as 'Not properly terminated' in xdist logs
The test cost is load-dependent and corpus-size-dependent, so future corpus growth can re-cross the timeout threshold without code changes

The fix chunk-parametrizes the equivalence test with fixed _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK size, ensuring each test case stays bounded and independent of corpus growth, enabling xdist to spread work across workers
A new coverage guard test asserts chunks reassemble to exactly _renderable_units and total >= 100, ensuring no units are silently dropped by parametrization
All 884 units remain compared against the oracle with real pandoc and _EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE stays 1, preserving the byte-identity property
